result.title: The Reference Matters: Displacement Probing for Weight-Space Learning
result.comment: 33 pages, 3 figures. (Equal contribution: Haechan Shin and Hoonki Lee)
result.summary: Weight-space learning predicts a model's attributes directly from its parameters, and probing-based methods do so efficiently by reading a model's responses to learned probes. Prior work shows that probing succeeds within a Model Tree -- models fine-tuned from a shared pretrained origin -- but not why. We trace this to the shared origin itself: since a tree's leaves start from the same weights, what distinguishes them is their displacement from that origin. This motivates probing the displacement rather than the raw weight, an intervention we call the DiSplacement Probe (DSProbe). We develop this idea along two axes: extending it to second-order Gram responses, whose displacement, to first order, tracks the feature changes induced by fine-tuning; and treating the reference as a design choice, learning a shared component to subtract beyond the pretrained origin. Across four architectures on the Model Jungle benchmark, the resulting Refined-DSProbe (R-DSProbe) sets a new state of the art, matches prior accuracy with substantially fewer probes, and supports a single encoder shared across Model Trees, reducing metanetwork parameters by 3.61 times. Code is available at https://github.com/hoonki2002/DSProbe.

AI.brief_summary: 论文追问 weight-space probing 为何只在共享预训练原点的 Model Tree 内有效，提出改而探测相对该原点的位移（DSProbe），并扩展到二阶 Gram 响应与可学习参考分量的 Refined-DSProbe，在 Model Jungle 基准上以更少 probe 取得更好精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先减去参考再比较差异」的思路可能为 latent 状态相似度分析提供参照：核查跨模型、跨深度或不同缓存条件下比较隐状态时，是否需先扣除共享基线才能暴露任务相关成分。
